claims.text: Catalytic activity in Pt/TiO2 catalysts is governed by nanoparticle-size-induced shifts in the Pt d-band center.
Catalytic selectivity in Pt/TiO2 catalysts is governed by nanoparticle-size-induced shifts in the Pt d-band center.
An optimal Pt nanoparticle size provides the most favorable adsorption energies for reactants and intermediates.
The Pt d-band center varies as a function of Pt nanoparticle size on TiO2.
XPS can characterize the proposed shifts in the Pt d-band center.
UV-vis spectroscopy can characterize the proposed shifts in the Pt d-band center.
Pt nanoparticles smaller or larger than the optimum have altered electronic structures.
Size-dependent electronic-structure changes shift the Pt d-band center relative to that of an intermediate-size particle.
Shifts in the Pt d-band center modify the adsorption energies of reactants and key intermediates.
The resulting adsorption-energy changes control catalytic activity and selectivity.
An intermediate Pt particle size, exemplified by 5 nm, will have greater catalytic activity than 2 nm and 10 nm particles.
An intermediate Pt particle size, exemplified by 5 nm, will have greater selectivity than 2 nm and 10 nm particles.
The proposed size–d-band–performance relationship is expected to hold for Pt/TiO2 under selective oxidation conditions at 200–300 °C.
Strong metal-support interactions beyond particle-size effects can dominate Pt/TiO2 catalytic behavior and limit the hypothesis.
Particle sintering can dominate catalytic behavior and limit the proposed relationship.
Synthesis variations and support effects can alter d-band-center shifts and catalytic performance.
Failure to observe both an intermediate-size performance optimum and a correlation between performance and d-band-center shifts would falsify the proposed governing mechanism.
